constraints: Resolve the human hallmark and human GO biological-process gene set collections from the environment's reference store at run time; confirm the organism is human before use

steps.description: Take the T2S1 results table for the treated vs control contrast and run pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) on the full gene ranking (shrunken log2FC, or sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) if shrinkage collapses the ranking), against two reference collections that must be resolved from the environment's reference store: the human hallmark gene sets and the human GO biological-process gene sets, both keyed on HGNC symbols. plan.title: Adipose RNA-seq: variance partition then treated vs control DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The dataset is a small bulk RNA-seq experiment in human adipose tissue: 12000 genes x 12 samples (counts.csv carries 13 columns — a gene-ID column plus 12 sample columns), with metadata.csv giving condition (6 treated vs 6 control), sex (F/M) and age (years) per sample, unpaired, single batch. The question has two parts in a fixed order, so the plan follows it.

T1S1 builds the analysis-ready object: match the 12 metadata rows to the 12 count columns by name, verify the 6/6 condition split, cross-tabulate condition against sex and check age by group so any confounding between the covariates and the treatment is on the table BEFORE any variance is attributed to them, filter low-count genes, and produce a VST/log-CPM matrix plus PCA for the variance work. Confounding diagnostics belong here because with n=6 per group a sex imbalance would make the sex variance fraction and the condition variance fraction partly the same number.

T1S2 answers part one directly with variancePartition: per-gene fractions of expression variance attributable to condition, sex, age and residual, fitted on the filtered VST/log-CPM matrix with observation weights from voom. All three predictors are fixed effects here — condition and sex are 2-level factors and age is continuous, none has enough levels for a random-effect fit — so the fractions are reported as fixed-effect variance fractions, and with only 12 samples and 4 model terms the per-gene estimates are noisy and are reported as a distribution across genes (median and IQR per term) rather than gene-by-gene claims.

T2S1 answers part two: DESeq2 on the raw Salmon counts, treated vs control. The design includes sex and age as covariates because the profile records them — but only if T1S1 shows they are estimable and not aliased with condition; the step must report both the covariate-adjusted and the condition-only fit so the reader can see what the adjustment cost or bought. Counts are gene-level from Salmon and the record does not state whether a length correction was applied, so the step treats them as a plain count matrix (round to integers, no tximport length offset) and says so explicitly, since applying an offset that was already applied is a silent error. Shrunken LFCs (apeglm) are used for ranking; independent filtering and BH FDR for calling.

T2S2 puts the DE result in biological context with a ranked GSEA against human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets staged locally — pre-ranked, on the full shrunken-LFC ranking rather than a thresholded list, because a 12-sample experiment may yield few or no genes past FDR 0.05 and a pre-ranked test still reads out coordinated shifts in that case. Gene identifier space in counts.csv is not recorded in the profile, so the step must detect it and map to HGNC symbols (local UniProt human ID mapping if the IDs are not already symbols), reporting the mapping rate.
